A_target.statement:
Let $f: M \to N$ be an $R$-[[Definition:Module Homomorphism|module homomorphism]].
Then:
:$M / \map \ker f \cong \Img f$
as $R$-[[Definition:Module|modules]].

B_source.statement:
Let $f: G \to H$ be a [[Definition:Group Homomorphism|group homomorphism]].
Then:
:$G / \map \ker f \cong \Img f$

validity_conditions: The additive group of a module is abelian, so ker(f) is automatically a submodule and the quotient module is well-defined.
The bijective-homomorphism argument transfers verbatim; the added obligation is checking the induced map respects the R-action.
proof_plan: $\map \ker f$ is a [[Definition:Submodule|submodule]] of $M$, the analogue of a [[Definition:Normal Subgroup|normal subgroup]].

Define $\bar f: M / \map \ker f \to \Img f$ by:
:$\map {\bar f} {m + \map \ker f} = \map f m$
The proof of the [[First Isomorphism Theorem for Groups]] shows $\bar f$ is well-defined and a [[Definition:Bijection|bijection]] of additive groups.

In addition, for $r \in R$:
:$\map {\bar f} {r \paren {m + \map \ker f} } = \map f {r m} = r \map f m$
so $\bar f$ is $R$-linear, and is a module [[Definition:Module Isomorphism|isomorphism]].
{{qed}}
